parsed.explanation: No universal exposure: the cross-dressing offence was struck down in 2018, and no document, facility, custody or care restriction touching visitors is sourced. Positives are substantial and documented: 72% acceptance (2022), pride parades held with police protection, government condemnation of attacks, police retraining with an equality body, and cross-party decriminalisation backing. Weighing against: inherited sodomy laws documented as a police extortion lever, residual vagrancy clauses usable against LGBT people, complainants facing secondary discrimination, no hate-crime statute, a 2017 courtroom exclusion of a trans victim with her case dismissed, and a 2018-2022 pattern of violence against trans women prompting regional-body urgent-action calls — real but without denominator, dated in parts, and met with institutional response rather than impunity. No organised targeting or tier-1 state exclusion is documented. Net: elevated friction and thin-to-partial recourse in a markedly accepting, reforming climate, mid-scale.
